title: Green peach aphids on round potato / Irish potato

Header: Green peach aphids on round potato / Irish potato

Prevention: Remove or plough under crop debris because it may host aphids.
However, if no major insect pests or diseases are in your crop, then do not plough and do not remove residues to avoid water loss.
Avoid growing the crop downwind from an infested field as aphids are blown by wind.
Consider breaking up large fields with strips of grain crops (e.g. millet).
This plant barrier “filters out” immigrating winged aphids and also restricts the movement of wingless aphids.
Apply grassy mulch and grow flowering plants to improve the environment for predator populations, e.g. lace wings, ladybird beetle or tiny parasitic wasps.
When in sufficient numbers they can effectively control the aphids.
Crop rotation as a preventive measure does not help much against flying insects like aphids.
Monitoring: Monitor the flight of winged aphids by weekly checking yellow sticky boards or yellow water pan traps placed along the field borders.
When aphids are captured on traps, start inspecting the field more carefully.
Inspect for shiny black eggs on the growing tips during the dry season.
When clusters of eggs are observed on buds of one potato plant per 10m² consider action
Later, visually inspect for both winged and wingless aphids underneath lower, yellowing leaves and buds of potato.
When 1 to 2 plants per 10m² are attacked by many such aphids, consider action.
Direct Control: Pick heavily infested leaves and bury outside field or compost well.
Wash aphids off with a hard spray from garden hose every 3-4 days.
Do not do this when potato diseases are in the field, because they will be spread
Ferment 20-50g marigold/ tagetes flowers / 1 litre water for 10 days stir daily; then filter and spray 1L/2L of water, max 3 sprays.
Soak 20-50g/L of water of neem cake/powder for 12-24 hours filter and spray.

Spray aphids with insecticidal soap:
Chop and grind or liquefy 1 garlic bulb and 1 small onion.
Add 1 teaspoon of powdered hot pepper and mix with 1 litre of water.
Steep 1 hour, strain through cheese cloth.
Then add 1 tablespoon of liquid dish soap to the strained liquid and mix well.
Spray plants thoroughly including leaf undersides.
Prepare the above ratio according to the size of the field at. 20 litres per acre.
A single spray should be applied over growing tips and leaves.
This is usually enough for aphid control.
If infestation continues, repeat application every other week as necessary.
The ingredient can cause painful skin and eye irritation.
